uncited: - **8-cube ($gs$):** A set of 8 voxels $v_0 \dots v_7$ ordered by binary coding of the index.
- **4-face:** One of the six inner faces of an 8-cube, composed of 4 voxels.
Each 4-face is shared by exactly two 8-cubes.
**Orientation:** Identify the six inner 4-faces for each 8-cube.
**Link Identification:** For each ordered 4-face, identify its four links (couples of 6-connected voxels).
- If link value is $(0,0)$ or $(1,1)$: No vertex is created.
- If link value is $(0,1)$: Create one vertex between the voxels; add an **incoming** oriented edge on this vertex staying on the 4-face.
**Handle Indeterminate Cases (4-configuration):** For 4-configurations 6 and 9, the result depends on the valid connectedness couple $(\eta, \lambda)$.
**Construct Local Graph:** Gather all oriented edges generated on the six oriented inner 4-faces to form the local graph $G_{gs}$ for the 8-cube.
**Construct Complete Graph:** Extend the set of all local graphs to form the complete graph $G(I)$.
**Triangulation:** Derive the final isosurface from the complete graph.
If loops have length $> 3$, they are subdivided (triangulated) to form a combinatorial manifold.
The choice of connectedness couple affects the surface shape.
- **When to use:** When topological correctness and consistency with the underlying voxel connectivity are critical.
- **When not to use:** When smoothness is more important than strict topological correctness, or when gradient data is available.
